<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919103_theRebbe_196" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919103_theRebbe_196__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Introductory header with the Torah portion and date.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Korach,</t>
    <t s="2">3 Tammuz 5718*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Explains that the life in which G-d placed our soul is above nature, preventing our foot from stumbling.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Hashem placed our soul in life, and did not give our foot to stumbling"1,</t>
    <t s="1">and it is explained by my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh" of the Festival of Redemption, 12 Tammuz2</t>
    <t s="2">[that the beginning of the redemption was on 3 Tammuz3],</t>
    <t s="3">that the life in which He placed our soul are levels of life higher than the life of the soul</t>
    <t s="4">(in and of itself).</t>
    <t s="5">For the life of the soul is limited,</t>
    <t s="6">for although the soul is inherently alive</t>
    <t s="7">(above the diffusion of vitality that enlivens the body,</t>
    <t s="8">and not only particular vitality but also general vitality)4,</t>
    <t s="9">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="10">since this that the soul is inherently alive is because the Holy One, blessed be He, implanted in the soul this nature</t>
    <t s="11">(that it should be inherently alive),</t>
    <t s="12">therefore,</t>
    <t s="13">even this vitality</t>
    <t s="14">(of the aspect of being inherently alive)</t>
    <t s="15">is within limitation,</t>
    <t s="16">and the life in which He placed our soul is above nature5.</t>
    <t s="17">And this is "Hashem placed our soul in life, and did not give our foot to stumbling,"</t>
    <t s="18">that the power for our feet not to stumble comes specifically from the life that is above nature.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Introduces the need to understand why the soul's own life can lead to stumbling, and connects this to the dispute of Korach and the firmament that separates.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And to understand the reason for this, that from the perspective of the life of the soul itself,</t>
    <t s="2">even from the aspect of being inherently alive,</t>
    <t s="3">it is possible for our foot to stumble,</t>
    <t s="4">and the power for our foot not to stumble comes specifically from the life that is above nature,</t>
    <t s="5">and also to understand the connection of this matter to the redemption of 12 Tammuz,</t>
    <t s="6">we must preface what is stated at the beginning of our parshah6:</t>
    <t s="7">"And Korach took," and Onkelos translated: "And Korach separated."</t>
    <t s="8">For wherever it says "vayikach" he translated "vensav," but here he translated "vesapleg."</t>
    <t s="9">And it is brought in the sefer Noam Elimelech7</t>
    <t s="10">that "vesapleg"</t>
    <t s="11">(Korach)</t>
    <t s="12">is like the firmament that separates between water and water.</t>
    <t s="13">And the Tzemach Tzedek explains8,</t>
    <t s="14">that this interpretation</t>
    <t s="15">(that "vesapleg Korach" is like the firmament that separates)</t>
    <t s="16">is based on what is brought in the Zohar9,</t>
    <t s="17">that the firmament that separates was a dispute of left with right, etc., like the dispute of Korach with Aharon.</t>
    <t s="18">From this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="19">that the connection of "vesapleg Korach" to the firmament that separates is not only because the root of dispute</t>
    <t s="20">(any dispute whatsoever)</t>
    <t s="21">is from the firmament that separates,</t>
    <t s="22">as it is brought in the Midrash10:</t>
    <t s="23">Why is "ki tov" not written on the second day? Because on it dispute was created, as it is said11,</t>
    <t s="24">"And it separated between water and water,"</t>
    <t s="25">but rather, even this particular dispute,</t>
    <t s="26">the dispute of Korach with Aharon,</t>
    <t s="27">is analogous to</t>
    <t s="28">(and its root is)</t>
    <t s="29">the dispute of the firmament that separates.</t>
    <t s="30">For just as the dispute of the firmament that separates is a dispute of left with right,</t>
    <t s="31">so too is the dispute of Korach with Aharon,</t>
    <t s="32">for Aharon is in the line of Chessed,</t>
    <t s="33">right,</t>
    <t s="34">and Korach, who was a Levite, was from the aspect of Gevuros,</t>
    <t s="35">left.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
